items.title: Verify and upgrade: Amazon FBA from China: model, rules and economics
items.question: Re-verify every fee, threshold and rule in [[Amazon FBA from China: Model, Rules and Economics]] against Amazon Seller Central and sell.amazon.ae pages (referral and FBA rate cards, subscription, storage, inbound from China, Brand Registry, drop shipping policy text), Dubai Customs and the Federal Tax Authority. The first version leaned on vendor articles. Raise confidence only where Tier 1 sources confirm.

result.summary: Re-verified against sell.amazon.ae, Dubai Customs, FTA and MoF: fees, duty, VAT thresholds and CT lines confirmed; import VAT handling and FBA fee corrected (net ~AED 34.55/unit before the Hormuz freight uplift); Seller Central eligibility rules still unverified (login-gated).

items.title: Best licence, entity, VAT and corporate tax set-up for an Amazon.ae private-label seller based in Dubai
items.question: Compare free zone e-commerce, mainland DET and any existing holdco route for a B2C Amazon.ae seller: licence activity, cost, Amazon acceptance, importer code, VAT registration timing, corporate tax (including whether B2C sales qualify for a free zone 0% rate under the current ministerial decisions, and Small Business Relief), banking and payouts in AED/USD. Give a recommended structure for a first-year seller and the questions to put to an adviser. Link to [[UAE Holding Structures]] and [[UAE Corporate Tax Essentials]].

result.summary: For a first-year B2C Amazon.ae seller a Dubai mainland DET LLC beats a free zone company because consumer sales are excluded from the free zone 0% rate; CT is nil at AED 400–600k revenue, but VAT likely becomes mandatory in year one because imports count towards the AED 375k threshold.

items.title: China sourcing playbook for a first-time private-label importer into the UAE
items.question: How to find, verify and manage factories on Alibaba, 1688, Global Sources and Made-in-China: licence verification services, factory vs trading company, Trade Assurance and escrow, sample strategy, MOQ negotiation, Incoterms, third-party inspection options and costs, tooling and IP protection, payment terms. Include door-to-FBA freight options to the UAE (sea and air), transit times, typical cost structure, and customs broker practice in Dubai. Cite sources and dates; use quotes ranges only from named providers.

result.summary: Verify licences yourself, pay 30/70 with the balance tied to a passed inspection (USD 268–298/man-day), file the trademark in China first, ship FOB/FCA under your own Dubai customs code, and budget ~AED 5/unit sea freight while Hormuz stays closed.

items.title: Which small, light, uncertified product categories look strongest on Amazon.ae and Noon right now?
items.question: Using public best-seller, new-release and trend data (and noting what could not be verified), identify 5 categories or niches with proven year-round demand, weak listings, low return rates and no certification burden. Include golf accessories as a candidate for the owner's beachhead. Give evidence with dates and flag seasonality (Ramadan, summer, back-to-school).

items.title: UAE and GCC product conformity and import rules by category for an Amazon seller
items.question: Which product types need conformity certification or registration before import or sale in the UAE (for example ECAS or other schemes), battery and dangerous-goods shipping rules, labelling (Arabic/English, origin, importer), restricted products, and how Amazon.ae gated categories interact. Produce a category-by-category checklist and say which authority to confirm with.

items.title: What a low-input Amazon store stack realistically looks like: tools, agencies, costs and hours
items.question: Document the automation stack for private-label sellers: Amazon native tools (automated pricing, ad rules, inventory alerts), listing and image services, PPC agencies, prep and freight forwarders, accounting. Give indicative cost ranges only from named providers, and sourced evidence on how many hours a week owners actually spend at different stages. Be explicit about what stays manual. Update [[Amazon FBA from China: Model, Rules and Economics]].

items.title: Expanding beyond Amazon.ae: Amazon.sa, Noon and a Shopify store from a UAE entity
items.question: Rules, fees, conformity and logistics for selling the same products on Amazon.sa, Noon and an own store from a UAE entity, including GCC shipping and customs and payment processing. When does diversification beat doubling down on one marketplace?

items.title: UAE holding structures for a family wealth & venture group: ADGM vs DIFC vs RAK ICC vs mainland
items.question: Which structure should hold ventures, property and investments? Compare setup and annual costs, substance and audit requirements, Corporate Tax treatment (incl. qualifying free zone rules), eligibility to hold Dubai property, banking practicality, succession benefits and privacy. Cite the official authority pages.

result.summary: Hold venture shares in a light ADGM/DIFC holdco, keep Dubai rental property personal or in a separate SPV because rent is non-qualifying income that can strip a free zone company of 0% status, and confirm DLD eligibility before buying via any entity.

items.title: Dubai property purchase costs and rental yield data: what are current DLD fees, and where to get reliable yield data by community?
items.question: Verify current transfer, registration and trustee fees and mortgage registration costs with the Dubai Land Department; explain how to use the RERA rental index and DLD transaction data to estimate net yields by community. Update [[Property Investment Metrics]].

result.summary: A mortgaged Dubai resale purchase costs ~7% of price in non-financeable fees (DLD 2%+2%, agency 2%+VAT, trustee, 0.25% mortgage registration); build net yields from DLD transaction, Ejari, Smart Rental Index and Service Charge Index data.

items.title: UAE Corporate Tax essentials for a founder with several small ventures
items.question: Registration, thresholds and rates, small business relief, free zone treatment, record-keeping and filing deadlines, and how this applies to an individual starting businesses. Primary source: tax.gov.ae.

result.summary: 0% to AED 375k then 9%; Small Business Relief (revenue ≤ AED 3m) extended to periods ending 31 Dec 2029; sole traders taxable above AED 1m combined turnover; register in 3 months, file/pay in 9, keep records 7 years.

items.title: Due diligence: Wednesday Circuit
items.question: Market for C-suite golf networking and corporate golf events in the UAE: number and capacity of championship courses, corporate day pricing benchmarks, competitors and membership-based networking models, licensing needed to sell events, and the riskiest assumptions to test first.

result.summary: Demand backdrop is strong but peak tee-time access at premier courses and willingness to pay over sponsor-funded incumbents (CEO Masters, FORE Business) are the first things to test.

items.title: Due diligence: DCS Golf
items.question: Luxury hand-made leather/canvas golf bags: price points of premium competitors, materials and supplier options (UAE vs import), unit cost structure for small-batch production, DTC and pro-shop channels in the GCC, and licensing for a home-based start.

result.summary: Hand-made bags sell at USD 850–1,200, but a UAE full-leather bag leaves ~27% DTC margin and losses via retail, and the home licences are officially for UAE/GCC nationals — lead with canvas+leather trim and corporate gifting.

items.title: Due diligence: Al Ain Ostrich Farm
items.question: Ostrich farming economics (birds, feed, mortality, meat/leather/feather yields), South African industry benchmarks (Oudtshoorn), UAE permits for livestock farming, slaughter and food service (ADAFSA, MOCCAE), agri-tourism demand in Al Ain, and capital required for a greenfield site.

result.summary: ADAFSA farm rules do not name ostriches, the Farm Licence is for Emirati owners, SA bird imports were banned in 2019, and Ostrich Oasis already runs the model in Al Ain — resolve permission and supply first and reframe around the visitor experience.

items.title: Confirm DLD's current policy on company and foundation ownership of Dubai freehold (ADGM, DIFC, RAK ICC, mainland)
items.question: DLD policy is unpublished and secondary sources conflict (e.g. ADGM foundations reportedly excluded). Get written/official confirmation, required documents and fees on later share transfers. Informs whether any property should ever sit in an entity.

items.title: Net yields for 3–5 target Dubai communities from DLD open data
items.question: Pull 12 months of DLD sales and Ejari rents plus Service Charge Index figures for shortlisted communities and compute net yield on total cost, versus current investment mortgage rates (EIBOR + margin). Informs the first purchase decision.

items.title: UAE VAT essentials for the three ventures
items.question: Mandatory/voluntary registration thresholds, timing, zero-rating/exemptions relevant to golf goods, events and agri-tourism/food, and interaction with e-invoicing from 1 Jul 2027. Primary source: tax.gov.ae.

items.title: Abu Dhabi farm tenure and ostrich permissions for a non-national operator
items.question: Can an expat lease or partner on an Al Ain farm; does ADAFSA permit ratites; current MOCCAE status on South African ostriches/hatching eggs; abattoir and restaurant licensing. Gates the Al Ain Ostrich Farm.

items.title: Dubai home-based and e-commerce licence options for an expat resident maker
items.question: DET eligibility for eTrader/Intelaq for residents, whether licences permit crafting/manufacturing at home, and free zone e-commerce alternatives with official prices. Gates DCS Golf.

items.title: Amazon.ae Seller Central requirements check (needs login)
items.question: With Seller Central access: current trade-licence rule, drop shipping policy text, subscription after the promotion, long-term storage and inbound fees, Amazon.ae payout currencies, and which trademark offices Brand Registry accepts (UAE MoE or not). Closes the unverified items in [[Amazon FBA from China: Model, Rules and Economics]].

items.title: Door-to-FBA freight quotes, China to Dubai, during the Hormuz closure
items.question: Written quotes from at least three named forwarders for 3–5 CBM LCL and air to Amazon.ae FBA, stating discharge port and trucking from Khor Fakkan/Fujairah, to replace the illustrative freight lines in the sourcing playbook and the Commerce Lab default.

items.title: Dubai mainland LLC vs Dubai CommerCity dual licence: all-in year-one cost
items.question: Real year-one and renewal cost of a DET e-commerce LLC (licence, Ejari/flexi-desk, approvals, Chamber) vs Dubai CommerCity with DET dual licence, from 2–3 written quotes, to finalise the Global Trend Store entity.

items.title: Verify the Incoterms 2020 table, UAE duty and import VAT treatment, and container specifications used in the Procurement engine
items.question: Check the Incoterms table in [[Procurement Fundamentals: Landed Cost, Incoterms and Negotiation]] cell by cell against the ICC's Incoterms 2020 text or an ICC-authored summary. Verify UAE customs duty basis (CIF) and typical rates, import VAT treatment, and Dubai Customs importer-code requirements against Dubai Customs and the Federal Tax Authority. Confirm 20ft, 40ft and 40ft high-cube internal volumes and payloads from a carrier or ISO-based source. Update the article and flag any change. Informs every venture that imports.

items.title: Materials and component suppliers for hand-made leather golf bags
items.question: Find reputable sources for full-grain and vegetable-tanned leather, waxed canvas, heavy-duty zips and hardware and rigid frames for a UAE luxury golf-bag maker. Give specification options, typical minimum orders, lead times and indicative price ranges with dates and sources. Cover UAE import duty and certification for leather, and traceability or sustainability claims to ask suppliers for. Label what is unverified.

items.title: Ostrich farm equipment, feed and import rules for the UAE
items.question: Cover fencing, feeders, incubation, veterinary and handling equipment, and feed for a greenfield ostrich farm in Al Ain. Include which items are normally imported (South Africa and elsewhere), the permits and veterinary conditions for importing birds, eggs and equipment into the UAE, and typical suppliers. Cite ADAFSA and Ministry of Climate Change and Environment sources first. A licensed adviser must confirm.

items.title: Event supplier cost benchmarks for corporate golf events in Dubai
items.question: Typical per-head and per-item cost ranges for breakfast catering, branded gifts, signage, trophies, audio-visual hire and photography for a C-suite golf event in the UAE, the supplier types to approach, and what to negotiate for recurring events. Cite sources and dates and say where figures are only indicative.

items.title: China to UAE freight rates, transit times and forwarder charges: benchmarks
items.question: Structure and indicative ranges (with dates and sources) for sea LCL, full-container and air freight from major Chinese ports to Jebel Ali, usual transit times, common forwarder and customs-broker charges, and what a door-to-door quote should and should not include. Flag what the owner must confirm with a forwarder.
